builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Wanda-Guided Sparse Perturbations for Efficient Zeroth-Order Optimization
summary: WIS-MeZO replaces MeZO's dense random perturbations in zeroth-order fine-tuning with sparse perturbations restricted to coordinates selected by Wanda weight-activation saliency, while keeping the pretrained weights dense. It adds a one-time saliency computation and mask construction, requires storing a sparse mask, and retains ZO's multiple forward passes per step; claimed benefit is fewer optimization steps to reach comparable validation loss. It can fail if the saliency-ranked support captures insufficient gradient energy for a given task, if the task-conditioning assumption breaks under distribution shift, or if sparse-gather overhead erodes the step-count savings in a memory-bound forward-only pipeline.
rationale: The method is directly implementable on a single 24 GB GPU for ZO fine-tuning of mid-size LLMs, but the claimed efficiency gain is step-count reduction without a quantified factor, so it warrants workload-specific A/B validation against plain MeZO before production adoption.

claims.statement: WIS-MeZO replaces MeZO's dense random perturbations in zeroth-order fine-tuning with sparse perturbations restricted to coordinates selected by Wanda weight-activation saliency, while keeping the pretrained weights dense. It adds a one-time saliency computation and mask construction, requires storing a sparse mask, and retains ZO's multiple forward passes per step; claimed benefit is fewer optimization steps to reach comparable validation loss. It can fail if the saliency-ranked support captures insufficient gradient energy for a given task, if the task-conditioning assumption breaks under distribution shift, or if sparse-gather overhead erodes the step-count savings in a memory-bound forward-only pipeline.
Higher aggregate scores than MeZO across 16 benchmarks on LLaMA/Qwen 3B-32B and comparable validation losses in fewer optimization steps; no multiplicative factor reported.
